description: The agency runs on it, and so does everyone it deals with.
Opens anything mechanical, given a minute nobody is watching.
The same job in a fraction of the time, at the cost of a noise.
Keeps the team on the same page. Trivial until it is missing.
Unglamorous, and the reason people come back from basements.
Overlays what the room is not telling you.
Ten seconds in a port buys a fortnight of somebody’s passwords.
Lifts and replays a print. Works on doors that trust fingers.
Turns a glass facade into a staircase.
Sees the room before anyone walks into it.
Walls stop being opaque. Guards stop being surprises.
Darkness becomes an advantage instead of a problem.
Be whoever the phone expects to hear.
Three floors in one movement, and it tells the time.
Through a safe door in ninety seconds. Single charge.
Somebody who is not there, standing exactly where you need them to look.
Everything the Smart Glasses do, with nothing to confiscate.
Crude, cheap, and enough for a camera at the wrong angle.
Two people leave the building. One of them went in.
Survives a bored official. Not a determined one.
Belongs to whichever staff list you need to be on.
Somebody else’s face, in about an hour.
Buys ten violent minutes and charges interest afterwards.
Turns an infection into an inconvenience.
Closes what is bleeding well enough to keep walking.
One guard, one nap, no paperwork.
Quiet, deniable, and hard to explain if searched.
Skips the interrogation and goes straight to the answer.
Lowers a guard’s judgement without lowering their pulse.
The exit plan for a building with no stairs left.
Leaves the perimeter without ever touching it.
Underwater, or through whatever they filled the room with.
Pockets well, argues convincingly.
Reach without noise.
Weighs nothing, passes every scanner, ends one conversation.
Built for the half-second after someone gets too close.
Ends a fight without ending a person.
Armour that reads as an accessory.
Impossible to conceal, and rarely necessary to draw twice.
Small, quiet, and entirely at home under a dinner jacket.
Boring, reliable, everywhere.
Heavier than it needs to be, and settles arguments accordingly.
One shot, no metal, no questions at the door.
Everyone in the building now knows where you are.
The standard answer when the plan has already failed.
Compact enough to carry under a coat, which it should not be.
Recoil goes down instead of up. Everything else goes down too.
Doors, locks, and the argument about whether to go in.
